[General] When `writeOpType` is `WRITE_OP_NONE` (reflection failure for all items) and `batchSize > 0`, the ternary `writeOpType == WRITE_OP_PUT ? "PutItem" : "DeleteItem"` silently defaults to `"DeleteItem"`. This is incorrect — if the type cannot be determined, the operation name should fall back to the raw `"BatchWriteItem"` rather than guessing `"DeleteItem"`.

While this scenario (reflection succeeds for counting but fails for classification) is extremely unlikely in practice, adding a guard for `WRITE_OP_NONE` makes the logic more robust and self-documenting.

threads.body: [General] The `WRITE_OP_NONE` fallback that was fixed in the SDK 2.2 extractor (line 90 of the v2.2 counterpart) is missing here. When `writeOpType` is `WRITE_OP_NONE` (reflection failed to classify the write requests) and `batchSize > 0`, the ternary on line 120 silently defaults to `"DeleteItem"` instead of falling back to `"BatchWriteItem"`. This is the exact same bug that was reported and fixed in the 2.2 version.
